answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with each step normalized by node degree. A sybil cluster arranged as a trellis, even if anchored by a wharf or falcon identity, gains little outside influence when its boundary is a sparse cut: low conductance limits walk flow across it. With capped per-attestation weight, min-cut and transitivity bounds therefore constrain the cluster’s aggregate voting weight instead of letting internal sybil links amplify it.
